source: Based on the topics of the Armenian grade 8 mathematics textbooks

stages.headline: There are infinite decimals that do not repeat; they are called irrational numbers.
stages.headlineEnglish: There are infinite decimals that do not repeat; they are called irrational numbers.

stages.headline: Rational numbers (finite or repeating decimals) and irrational numbers together form the real numbers R.
stages.headlineEnglish: Rational numbers (finite or repeating decimals) and irrational numbers together form the real numbers R.

stages.headline: √2 is not rational: if √2 = p/q in lowest terms, then p² = 2q², so p is even, then q is even too — a contradiction.
stages.headlineEnglish: √2 is not rational: if √2 = p/q in lowest terms, then p² = 2q², so p is even, then q is even too — a contradiction.

stages.headline: Write two irrational numbers whose sum is rational.
stages.headlineEnglish: Write two irrational numbers whose sum is rational.
stages.problemText: Write two irrational numbers whose sum is rational.
stages.customInstructions: Any correct pair is accepted, e.g. √2 and 1 − √2.
